text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate detected for production in eu-west-1. Auto-traffic-shift to eu-central-1 triggered by failover-policy v3.2.

portal-monitor: metric spike: 5xx rate 12% (baseline 0.3%), p95 latency 2.8s, request drop on egress from eu-west-1 AZ2.

alex.sre: acked. I'm oncall. Investigating. Paging networking and infra.

maya.infra: looking. I'm seeing healthchecks flapping on several NLB targets in eu-west-1-A. Logs show repeated connection reset + TLS handshake timeouts.

kevin.net: joining. Checking inter-AZ route tables and peering. Initial dig + traceroute from our external probe -> some hops time out near the provider edge in eu-west-1-A. Could be partial fabric outage.

alex.sre: are customer-facing DNS entries being updated correctly during the automated shift? Any TTL weirdness?

kevin.net: our traffic-shift uses weighted DNS + ALB routing via geoproximity. TTL is 30s. But I see a handful of AS paths still advertising the old prefix for eu-west-1-A. Some ISPs might be routing into a blackholed path.

maya.infra: stack traces from instances show heavy CPU on the request path, then kernel drops. Could be network-level packet loss causing retries and overload loops (draining loop).

alex.sre: ok, mitigation plan: (1) pause automated rollouts to eu regions, (2) force a broad traffic-shift to us-east-1 for read/serve endpoints, (3) coordinate with cloud provider for AZ fabric.

kevin.net: agreed. I can push a manual override to route primary traffic to us-east-1 and increase grace for connection draining. Command I'm about to run: ```/infra traffic-shift --from eu-west-1 --to us-east-1 --force --override-policy=immediate```

maya.infra: before you run it, confirm health-probe drain settings. If we move traffic too fast we might overload us-east. Suggest 10% step with 30s waits.

kevin.net: noted. I'll start with 25% steps to reduce blast radius. Starting now.

incident-bot: ACTION: manual traffic-shift initiated by kevin.net at 1741210200. Target: us-east-1. Mode: stepped weights (25% increments).

support-bot: customer alert: increased error rates for some tenants. Drafting status msg.

alex.sre: can someone run quick end-to-end synthetics against the new primary region and confirm tokenization/embedding endpoints?

maya.infra: curl check: ```curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Region: us-east-1'``` returned `200 0.42s` from 3/3 probes. Good.

kevin.net: step 1 -> 25% shifted. Observing connection queue growth in us-east-1 but within headroom. External traceroute from probe now reaches us-east-1 without loss.

alex.sre: good. keep stepping, but watch for queuing and p95 latency. Notify me if p95 > 1s or CPU > 60% on any serving pool.

portal-monitor: after step 2 (50%): error rate dropped to 3.1% overall. p95 0.7s.

maya.infra: I'm seeing a repeat pattern: some eu-west-1 load balancers are stuck draining targets then re-registering -> unhealthy -> drain loop. That's what triggered auto-shift. I've temporarily blocked the health-checks to stop churn while we coordinate with provider. Command: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:tg:eu-west-1:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false```

kevin.net: provider (cloud-NOC) responded: they're investigating metro fabric in eu-west-1-A, BGP convergence issues. They recommend customers do not shift traffic back until fabric stable.

alex.sre: Thanks. Given provider guidance, leave primary in us-east-1 for now. Start drafting postmortem and customer impact summary.

support-bot: customer post: "We are investigating increased 5xxs in EU and have temporarily shifted traffic to US while cloud provider resolves a regional fabric issue. No action required from customers; suppressed retries recommended." Will push in 5 min. :loudspeaker:

irene.sre: I'm taking over on-call at 1741213800 for a 2h window. Quick handoff notes: auto-traffic-shift fired due to NLB drain loop in eu-west-1-A. Manual override to us-east-1 done (50% -> 100% in stepped plan). Provider fabric outage suspected. Monitoring: watch p95, cpu, and error-rate; support already notified customers.

alex.sre: thanks irene. I have to jump to a meeting. Handoff acked. Full notes in convo.

irene.sre: ack. I'll keep pages if anything deteriorates. Next steps: 1) provider incident #CN-94112 watch, 2) keep traffic pinned to us-east-1, 3) coordinate with infra to unstick NLB registrations once fabric stable, 4) prepare rollback play if provider says stable but we still see flapping.

kevin.net: small note — we saw a subset of customers (enterprise-tenant ids A12, B45) with long-lived BGP sessions to the failed AS that still route into eu-west-1-A. We're adding a short-lived AS-path prepending on our edge prefixes to steer them out.

maya.infra: logs show no data plane corruption, just packet loss -> service timeouts -> client retries -> load spike -> drain loop. So mitigation is network-first.

portal-monitor: current metrics at 1741215600: global 5xx 0.6% (down from 12%), eu-west-1 5xx 1.9% (from 14%), p95 global 0.65s.

support-bot: customer update posted. Escalation channel opened with provider.

irene.sre: creating incident ticket INC-2026-042 in ops board and assigning to oncall-runbook. I'll draft postmortem skeleton and include timeline + mitigation actions.

alex.sre: FYI for postmortem: include detection: auto-failover metrics, decision to manual override, provider communications, customer impact list (tenants with >10% errors), and mitigation commands used.

kevin.net: once provider confirms fabric stable, we'll test a slow re-introduction to eu regions with small weights and watch for NLB churn. We should also add a guard to prevent immediate canary rollouts into an AZ with recent healthcheck churn (rate-limit canary by region).

maya.infra: agree. Also add an infra monitor for target-group registration churn > X per 5m to trigger early alert.

irene.sre: logging note: transcript will be saved to INC-2026-042. Closing active paging unless error-rate rises above 2% global.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: incident marked as mitigated (manual traffic-shift + provider coordination). Status: monitoring.

alex.sre: thanks all. If things look stable in 1h, we'll move to write a customer-facing RCA draft.

kevin.net: :thumbsup:
